messages:
incbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert INC-7321 triggered for prod - high error rate and crashlooping pods in namespace=redwood-inference, deployment=inference-canary. Affected region: us-west-2. On-call: alex-oncall

alex-oncall: I’m on it. Paging SRE and the deploy authoring team. any recent rollouts?

deploy-bot: Deploy event: user=maria-eng started rollout inference-canary:v2 -> v3 at 2141589950 (automated canary dims: 10%). Change: enable new encoder, adjust HPA target CPU to 65% in manifest.
maria-eng: yep that was me - feature flag rollout + small HPA tweak. I ran a quick smoke locally, looked fine.

jon-sre: seeing CrashLoopBackOff on pods: inference-canary-684c6b7f*. Logs show repeated "failed to mmap model shard: out of memory" and then process OOMKilled. sample log:
```
2026-03-15T08:12:31Z stderr model_loader.cpp:142] mmap failed: Cannot allocate memory
2026-03-15T08:12:31Z kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2345 (runner) score 987 or sacrifice child
```

alex-oncall: that fits a memory regression. Could be the new encoder using more resident memory than expected. Let's stop canary traffic and flip the flag off. maria, can you kill the flag?
maria-eng: initiating kill-switch. Using ff-service to set rollout.enable_new_encoder=false for prod. command:
```
ffctl set rollout.enable_new_encoder false --env=prod --actor=maria-eng --reason="paging - crashloops"
```

maria-eng: done — flag toggled to false. deploy-bot: Canary traffic drained to 0%.

jon-sre: Pods still CrashLoopBackOff on nodes that already pulled the v3 image; new flag flip prevents new pods from switching but existing ones are still OOMing on restart. Suggest `kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-canary --to-revision=2` to get back to v2 image and manifest.
alex-oncall: go ahead with rollback, jon. Also scale HPA to 0 for canary so it doesn't keep creating pods while we stabilize. commands: 
```
kubectl -n redwood-inference scale deployment inference-canary --replicas=0
kubectl -n redwood-inference rollout undo deployment/inference-canary --to-revision=2
```

jon-sre: scaled to 0, rollout undo issued. rollout status shows: "deployment "inference-canary" successfully rolled back to revision 2". Now scaling back to expected baseline 2 replicas.

ops-bot: Incident impact summary: 12% of inference API requests errored for ~7 minutes (08:12 - 08:19 PT). Affected customers: subset of low-latency canaries; no enterprise customers on dedicated capacity impacted (per routing logs). Temporary rate-limit fallback triggered for some clients.

janet-cs: I’ve opened a ticket for a couple of small customers who reported increased error rates. I can send a short status update once we have stabilization timeframe.

maria-eng: root cause hypothesis: encoder v3 increases memory pressure due to a change in shard loading (mmap instead of streaming) + HPA tweak allowed more concurrent pods with higher mem use. Repro steps: local dev repro with smaller mem limit shows same mmap failure.

alex-oncall: next actions: 1) keep rollout flag off 2) revert HPA target to previous 50% 3) postmortem assignment to maria-eng; SRE to review node-level memory eviction patterns (jon). I’ll start a bridge for postmortem notes.
maria-eng: I’ll own the postmortem and follow up with a safe re-roll plan (gradual mem profiling, heap cap, and canary with memory telemetry).

jon-sre: I’ll check cluster nodes for any leftover oom/killed processes and confirm no persistent node-level instability. preliminary check: two nodes had transient swap/memory pressure but both recovered, no cordons needed.

alex-oncall: Handoff: I’m handing incident to maria-eng for the postmortem and remediation. I’m going offline for 30m. If it resurfaces, re-page pagerduty with high urgency. :white_check_mark:

maria-eng: ack, will own. Adding follow-ups: revert HPA change, add memory-usage alert for inference-canary above 70%, add a pre-rollout mem-sanity check in CI.

ops-bot: Incident closed for now — service returned to healthy baseline and errors dropped to <0.1%. Start time: 2141590001, mitigation complete: 2141590360.

janet-cs: thanks — I’ll send customers a short note summarizing the rollback and expected follow-up.

alex-oncall: thanks team, nice quick mitigation.
